```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(shiny)
library(readr)       # for importing data
library(vip)         # for variable importance plots
library(janitor)     # for tabyl
library(forcats)     # for factor operations
library(tidymodels)
library(tidyverse)
library(modelr)
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(broom)
library(ggfortify)
library(performance)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(dplyr)
library(skimr)
library(rsample)
library(themis)
library(yardstick)
library(xgboost)
library(bslib)
library(shinydashboard)
library(skimr)

# Import data
dataRaw <- read_csv("healthcare.csv")
dataClean <- dataRaw %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  mutate(
    ever_married    = if_else(ever_married == "Yes", 1L, 0L),
    residence_type  = if_else(residence_type == "Urban", 1L, 0L),
    gender          = if_else(gender == "Male", 1L, 0L),
    stroke          = factor(stroke, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
    work_type       = as.factor(work_type),
    smoking_status  = as.factor(smoking_status),
    bmi             = as.numeric(na_if(bmi, "N/A"))
  )

dataClean2 <- dataClean %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  filter(smoking_status != "Unknown")

```

#### Prediction:
```{r side_bar2}
sliderInput("age", "Age:", min = 0, max = 100, value = 50)

selectInput("gender", "Gender:", choices = c("Male" = 1, "Female" = 0))

selectInput("smoking", "Smoking Status:", 
            choices = levels(dataClean$smoking_status))

selectInput("work", "Work Type:", choices = levels(dataClean$work_type))

selectInput("residence", "Residence Type:", choices = c("Urban" = 1, "Rural" = 0))

sliderInput("bmi", "BMI:", min = 10, max = 60, value = 25)

checkboxInput("married", "Ever Married?", TRUE)

actionButton("predict", "Predict Stroke Risk")
```

### **Project Description**

```{r}
htmltools::div(
  style = "background-color:#1a1a1a; padding:20px; border-radius:10px; color:white;",
  HTML("<h4>About This Project</h4><p>According to the World Health Organization (WHO) stroke is the 2nd leading cause of death globally, responsible for approximately 11% of total deaths.

This data set is used to predict whether a patient is likely to get stroke based on the input parameters like gender, age, various diseases, and smoking status. Each row in the data provides relevant information about the patient.</p>")
)
```
